exact_statement.abstract: Let V be a finite-dimensional real vector space, Lambda a full lattice, C != V a full-dimensional closed convex cone, and c in Int_V(C) intersect Lambda. If (Int_V(C)-c) intersect Lambda is contained in C, then C is an intersection of finitely many halfspaces eta_i >= 0 with primitive eta_i in Lambda* and eta_i(c)=1. Consequently C is rational polyhedral and every primitive nonnegative facet form has height one at c.
exact_statement.saturation: If Gamma is contained in K intersect Lambda, K satisfies the abstract cone hypotheses, c is an interior lattice point, and for every q in Lambda the implication q+c in Int K => q in Gamma holds, then K has primitive height-one rational facets, Gamma=K intersect Lambda, and Int K intersect Lambda=c+Gamma. In the inherited jet setting Gamma is finitely generated, saturated, and has group Lambda.
exact_statement.version_1_comparison: Version 2 removes the specified bounded-degree-slice epigraph, exponent orthant, degree coordinate and jet-semigroup structure of version 1 by constructing a global epigraph along c. It also permits lineality. The preserved final proof supports both versions; no separate earlier version-1 proof is represented as independently checked.

hypotheses.proper_convention: The report has no separate pointedness definition. Only C != V is needed to choose a nonzero nonnegative support; the proof is verified under this weaker convention.

hypotheses.lineality: After the proof, L=C intersect (-C)=intersection_i ker eta_i is rational and has dimension from 0 to dim(V)-1. The quotient is pointed; rationality is not assumed to form a lattice quotient in advance.
hypotheses.edge_cases: Dimension one is the ray case and forces c to be its primitive lattice generator. W=ker ell then has dimension zero. Dimension zero is vacuous under C != V. Rays in higher-dimensional ambient spaces are excluded by full dimensionality.
geometric_application: Gamma is contained in K intersect Lambda, with K the full-dimensional proper closed cone of actual Taylor initials.
Lambda={(j,alpha) in Z x Z^N: j congruent sum_i b_i alpha_i modulo m}.
The canonical character identity r congruent sum_i b_i modulo m puts c=(r,1,...,1) in Lambda.
c in Int K is an additional independent hypothesis.
The exact lifting implication holds for all q in Lambda, not only finitely many or asymptotically.
hypotheses.coordinate_qualification: The lattice has index m, with basis (m,0) and (b_i,e_i) for integer representatives b_i. Degree is the original j. The integration change j -> Nj/r transports the lattice and c to the image lattice and (N,1,...,1); it does not authorize replacing that image lattice by the standard integer lattice.

decisive_findings.finding: A nonzero ell in the dual cone normalized by ell(c)=1 gives C={x+s c: s>=g(x)} on all W=ker ell. Interior c makes every fiber nonempty above, and ell gives its lower bound. No pointedness, compact primal slice or lattice on W is required.

At a differentiability point, the support eta has eta(c)=1. If its lattice image is not Z, it is either dense or hZ with 1=kh and k>1; both give w with -1<eta(w)<0. Torus recurrence near multiples of the boundary point and the differentiability estimate produce a lattice q outside C but q+c inside Int C.
decisive_findings.effect: proves primitive integrality and height one for every smooth-point support

decisive_findings.finding: A ball about c bounds every normalized nonnegative support by 1/epsilon. Only its integral members are finite, by dual-lattice discreteness. Neither primal slices nor forbidden strips are assumed bounded; arbitrary real supports at nonsmooth points need not be integral.
decisive_findings.effect: validates the precise finiteness step without a finite-search inference
